choices.choice: Time-lag design using three cross-sections 15 years apart from a national school survey
Use of Forms 3 and 4 only; no sample exclusions
No sampling weights and no design-based variance adjustment
Dropping two two-item factors for alpha < .50 and re-fitting a five-factor model
Not scaling the Form 3 work-centrality items because of poor CFA fit and low alpha; item-level t tests instead
Multigroup invariance sequence with delta CFI .002 criterion (Meade et al.) preferred over chi-square difference
Partial scalar invariance with six freed intercepts including one of the two altruistic items
Reporting latent means on the item metric for all groups with LISREL SEs and 95% CIs; effect sizes d without a stated formula
Significance of latent mean differences judged from effect sizes/CIs rather than reported pairwise tests
Item-level independent t tests with stars; variance assumption and n not stated

undocumented_items_list: assignment of dropped items to security/influence and of Form 3 items to centrality/stability

unusualness_rating: 2 - The design and invariance workflow are conventional for the field; the unusual elements are reporting latent means on the raw item metric with d values whose formula is unstated, judging pairwise significance from CIs/effect sizes without pairwise tests, and text/table discrepancies (5-point vs 4-point scale; reliabilities said to be in Table 1 but absent).

documentation_scores.rationale: Items, forms, years, factor assignments, freed intercepts and software are specified; missing data, weights, estimator, d formula, SD definition and item-level n are not; Table 1 reproduces all means/SDs/percentages/t and Table 2 all fit statistics, but alphas for retained scales are promised and absent, and the Form 4 response scale is misdescribed.
